questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyzes the following reaction:

$\begin{array}{cc} X & Y \\ | & | \\ C & - & C \end{array} \rightarrow X-Y + C=C$
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 11 | Page: 117 | Paragraph: 6

The given reaction involves the removal of groups $X$ and $Y$ from the substrate, resulting in the formation of a double bond between the carbon atoms.

Enzymes that catalyze the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds, are classified as lyases.

Hydrolases catalyze the cleavage of bonds by the addition of water.

Isomerases catalyze the interconversion of optical, geometric, or positional isomers.

Ligases catalyze the joining together of two molecules.

Thus, the enzyme catalyzing the given reaction belongs to the class lyase.

Answer: (2) Lyase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the type of placentation in Column I with its corresponding structural characteristic and plant example in Column II.
Column IColumn II
(a) Axile(i) False septum formation in a unilocular ovary; Mustard
(b) Parietal(ii) Single ovule attached at the ovary base; Sunflower
(c) Free central(iii) Multilocular ovary with central attachment; Lemon
(d) Basal(iv) Septa are completely absent; Dianthus
Select the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 11 | Page: 65 | Paragraph: 2

Axile placentation occurs in a multilocular ovary where ovules are attached to the central axis. Example: Lemon. Thus, (a) matches (iii).

Parietal placentation occurs when ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary. A false septum may form, making the unilocular ovary bilocular. Example: Mustard. Thus, (b) matches (i).

Free central placentation features ovules borne on a central axis with septa completely absent. Example: Dianthus. Thus, (c) matches (iv).

Basal placentation involves a single ovule attached at the base of the ovary. Example: Sunflower. Thus, (d) matches (ii).

The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

Answer: (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological sequence regarding the development of a mature male gametophyte from a microspore mother cell (MMC) in a typical angiosperm:

I. Asymmetric mitotic division of the microspore nucleus.
II. Meiotic division of the microspore mother cell.
III. Dissociation of the microspore tetrad.
IV. Mitotic division of the generative cell to form two male gametes.
V. Formation of a large vegetative cell and a small generative cell.
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 6 - 7 | Paragraph: 1 - 2

The development of a mature male gametophyte from a microspore mother cell (MMC) in a typical angiosperm follows a specific sequence of events:

The microspore mother cell (MMC) first undergoes meiotic division to form a cluster of four cells called a microspore tetrad (Event II).

As the anther matures and dehydrates, the microspores dissociate from the tetrad and develop into individual pollen grains (Event III).

Inside the pollen grain, the microspore nucleus undergoes an asymmetric mitotic division (Event I).

This asymmetric division results in the formation of two unequal cells: a large vegetative cell and a small spindle-shaped generative cell (Event V).

Finally, the generative cell undergoes a second mitotic division to produce two non-motile male gametes, completing the formation of a mature three-celled male gametophyte (Event IV).

The correct chronological sequence is II \rightarrow III \rightarrow I \rightarrow V \rightarrow IV.

Answer: II \rightarrow III \rightarrow I \rightarrow V \rightarrow IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I (Utilisation Category) with List-II (Examples/Definitions):

List-IList-II
(A) Narrowly Utilitarian(I) Oxygen production and Pollination
(B) Broadly Utilitarian(II) $25,000$ species of plants used for medicine
(C) Ethical Argument(III) Exploring molecular/genetic level diversity for products
(D) Bioprospecting(IV) Philosophically sharing the planet with all species

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 223 - 224 | Paragraph: 5,6 - 1,2

Narrowly utilitarian arguments for conserving biodiversity are based on direct economic benefits derived from nature, such as food, firewood, fibre, and medicines. More than $25,000$ species of plants are used in traditional medicines. Thus, (A) matches with (II).

Broadly utilitarian arguments are based on the ecosystem services provided by nature, such as oxygen production and pollination. Thus, (B) matches with (I).

The ethical argument relates to the philosophical and spiritual realization that we share the planet with millions of other species, each having an intrinsic value. Thus, (C) matches with (IV).

Bioprospecting is the exploration of molecular, genetic, and species-level diversity to obtain products of economic importance. Thus, (D) matches with (III).

The correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (1) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following about the Lac operon are CORRECT?
(I) The lac operon in E. coli consists of a regulatory gene (lacI), a promoter, an operator, and three structural genes: lacZ ($\beta$-galactosidase), lacY (permease), lacA (transacetylase).
(II) In the absence of lactose, the repressor protein binds to the operator and prevents transcription.
(III) Lactose (the inducer) directly binds to the operator, displacing the repressor.
(IV) The lac operon is an example of negative regulation - the repressor is the negative regulator.
(V) Each gene codes as such; lacZ ($\beta$-galactosidase), lacY (permease), lacA (transacetylase).
options: I, II, IV and V only
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 100-101 | Paragraph: 4 - 1,2

Statement (I) is correct as the lac operon consists of one regulatory gene (the i gene) and three structural genes (z, y, and a).

Statement (II) is correct as the repressor protein synthesized from the i gene binds to the operator region of the operon in the absence of an inducer and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon.

Statement (III) is incorrect because lactose (or allolactose) acts as an inducer by binding to the repressor protein, not the operator. This binding inactivates the repressor, preventing it from binding to the operator.

Statement (IV) is correct as the regulation of the lac operon by a repressor is referred to as negative regulation.

Statement (V) is correct as the z gene codes for $\beta$-galactosidase, the y gene codes for permease, and the a gene codes for transacetylase.

Thus, statements (I), (II), (IV), and (V) are correct.

Answer: (3) I, II, IV and V only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The core of a nucleosome consists of an octamer of histone molecules, which acquire their positive charge due to an abundance of basic amino acid residues like lysine and arginine.

Statement II: At a higher level of packaging, regions of chromatin that are densely packed and stain dark are called euchromatin, and they represent the transcriptionally inactive parts of the genome.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 11 | Page: 76 - 77 | Paragraph: 3- 1,2,44

Statement I is correct because the nucleosome core is formed by a histone octamer. Histones are rich in basic amino acid residues, specifically lysine and arginine, which give them a positive charge to tightly bind the negatively charged DNA.

Statement II is incorrect because densely packed and dark-staining regions of chromatin are called heterochromatin, which is transcriptionally inactive. Euchromatin, on the other hand, is loosely packed, stains light, and is transcriptionally active.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Arrange the following fundamental steps of DNA fingerprinting in the correct chronological order:
A. Digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases
B. Separation of DNA fragments by gel electrophoresis
C. Hybridisation using a radiolabelled VNTR probe
D. Transferring of separated DNA fragments to a synthetic membrane
E. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 106 | Paragraph: 2

The fundamental steps of DNA fingerprinting are carried out in the following sequence:

1. Isolation of DNA.

2. Digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases (A).

3. Separation of DNA fragments by gel electrophoresis (B).

4. Transferring (blotting) of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes, such as nitrocellulose or nylon (D).

5. Hybridisation using a radiolabelled VNTR probe (C).

6. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography (E).

Thus, the correct chronological order is A \rightarrow B \rightarrow D \rightarrow C \rightarrow E.

Answer: A \rightarrow B \rightarrow D \rightarrow C \rightarrow E

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If a man with blood group AB marries a woman with blood group O, what blood groups can be expected in their offspring?
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 61 | Paragraph: 2

The genotype of the man with blood group AB is $I^A I^B$.

The genotype of the woman with blood group O is $i i$.

The gametes produced by the man are $I^A$ and $I^B$.

The gamete produced by the woman is $i$.

Crossing the gametes, the possible genotypes of the offspring are $I^A i$ and $I^B i$.

The genotype $I^A i$ corresponds to blood group A, and the genotype $I^B i$ corresponds to blood group B.

Therefore, the expected blood groups in their offspring are A and B only.

Answer: (2) A and B only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I (Biological Structures) with List-II (Anatomical Origin and Evolutionary Pattern):
List-IList-II
A. Sweet potato and potatoI. Homologous structures representing modification of axillary buds (Divergent evolution)
B. Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of CucurbitaII. Analogous structures where root and stem are respectively modified for storage (Convergent evolution)
C. Forelimbs of whales and batsIII. Analogous structures with different anatomical origins adapted for aquatic life (Convergent evolution)
D. Flippers of Penguins and DolphinsIV. Homologous structures sharing common tetrapod ancestry adapted for different functions (Divergent evolution)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 114 -115 | Paragraph: 1 - 1

Sweet potato is a root modification and potato is a stem modification. Both perform the same function of storage of food, making them analogous structures resulting from convergent evolution. Thus, A matches II.

Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita are both modifications of axillary buds. They share a common anatomical origin but perform different functions (protection and climbing, respectively), making them homologous structures resulting from divergent evolution. Thus, B matches I.

Forelimbs of whales and bats share a common tetrapod ancestry and have the same basic skeletal structure but are adapted for different functions (swimming and flying). They are homologous structures resulting from divergent evolution. Thus, C matches IV.

Flippers of penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) have different anatomical origins but perform the same function of swimming. They are analogous structures resulting from convergent evolution. Thus, D matches III.

The correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
With respect to drug abuse, identify the correct statements from the following:

A. Heroin is chemically diacetylmorphine, which acts as a depressant and slows down body functions.
B. Natural cannabinoids are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system of the body.
C. Cocaine interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine and produces a sense of euphoria.
D. Morphine is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant Papaver somniferum and is an effective sedative for surgical patients.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 142 - 143 | Paragraph: 5 - 1,2

Statement A is correct. Heroin, commonly called smack, is chemically diacetylmorphine. It is a depressant and slows down body functions.

Statement B is correct. Natural cannabinoids are obtained from the inflorescences of the plant Cannabis sativa. They are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system of the body.

Statement C is correct. Cocaine is obtained from the coca plant Erythroxylum coca. It interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine, producing a sense of euphoria and increased energy.

Statement D is correct. Morphine is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant Papaver somniferum. It is a very effective sedative and painkiller, making it highly useful for patients who have undergone surgery.

Since all statements are correct, the correct choice includes A, B, C, and D.

Answer: A, B, C and D

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The correct sequence of events in the life cycle of Plasmodium is:

A. Parasites reproduce asexually in the liver cells and then burst into the blood.
B. Fertilization and development take place in the mosquito's gut.
C. Sporozoites are injected into the human body through a mosquito bite.
D. Gametocytes are taken up by a female Anopheles mosquito during a blood meal.
E. Parasites reproduce asexually in red blood cells, causing them to rupture and release hemozoin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 132 | Diagram

The life cycle of Plasmodium starts when an infected female Anopheles mosquito bites a healthy human, injecting the infective stage, sporozoites, into the human body (C).

The sporozoites reach the liver through the blood, where they reproduce asexually in the liver cells, bursting the cells and releasing the parasites into the blood (A).

These parasites then enter the red blood cells (RBCs) and reproduce asexually, causing the RBCs to rupture. The rupture of RBCs is associated with the release of a toxic substance called hemozoin, which is responsible for the chill and high fever (E).

Some of the parasites in the RBCs differentiate into sexual stages called gametocytes. When a female Anopheles mosquito bites the infected person, these gametocytes are taken up along with the blood meal (D).

Inside the mosquito's body, fertilization and further development of the gametes take place in the gut, forming sporozoites which migrate to the salivary glands (B).

The correct sequence of events is C, A, E, D, B.

Answer: (1) C, A, E, D, B

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Restriction endonucleases function by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence to find and bind to a specific recognition sequence.
Statement II: These enzymes cut the strand of DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome sites, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 166 - 167 | Paragraph: 2 - 2

Statement I is correct. Each restriction endonuclease functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence. Once it finds its specific recognition sequence, it binds to the DNA and cuts each of the two strands of the double helix at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbones.

Statement II is correct. Restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome sites, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands. This leaves single-stranded portions at the ends, which are called sticky ends.

Therefore, both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Answer: Both statement I and statement II are correct
